title: You are the form of light
word: You are the form of light
hook: man too jot saroop hai: O mind, you are the form of light; know your origin (Asa M3, ang 441)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the old Guru's voice: Guru Amar Das, patient with the wandering mind, saying ego and the Name won't fit in one place. When did the I, I, mine get loud? Day one thousand one hundred eighty-three.

Man too jot saroop hai. A short run of Punjabi that lands like a hand on the shoulder. Yesterday we heard Guru Amar Das talking to the mind the way you'd talk to someone who keeps drifting off. Today he stops calling it home for a moment and tells it what it is. Not a problem to fix. Not a list of failures. A form of light. It's in Raga Asa, on Ang four hundred forty-one of the Guru Granth Sahib, and it opens by addressing the mind directly: man too. O mind, you.
screen: `MAN TOO JOT SAROOP HAI.` → `NOT A PROBLEM TO FIX.` → `O MIND, YOU.`

segments.voice: Here's the line, paraphrased: O my mind, you are the very form of light; recognize your own origin. Jot is light, the same word Sikhs use for the light that passed from Guru to Guru. Saroop is form, shape, likeness. Mool is root, origin, where something starts. So the line holds a picture and an instruction. The picture: what you are, underneath the noise, is light. The instruction: go find out where it came from. Then the hymn goes on, again paraphrased: O mind, the Lord is with you; through the Guru's teaching, enjoy that love. Recognize your origin and you'll know your Lord, and understand dying and living. Notice the order. It doesn't say you are the Lord, so stop looking. It says you are light, so look for the source of the light. Recognizing yourself and recognizing your Lord turn out to be one road. That fits the week behind us. Guru Angad called the Guru a light in the darkness. He warned that service can carry pride, and that ego is an illness with its cure inside. Guru Amar Das said ego and the Name can't share a room. And now, the reason the room is worth clearing: what lives there is light. Some readers hear this line as the quiet center of all the warnings. The warnings about ego aren't there because the mind is worthless. They're there because it's made of something precious and keeps forgetting.
screen: `JOT, SAROOP, MOOL.` · `LIGHT, FORM, ORIGIN.` · `KNOW YOUR ROOT, KNOW YOUR LORD.` · `WHY THE WARNINGS MATTER.` · then, large: `YOU ARE LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember your origin. Settle, and let the breath slow. On the in-breath, let the words come quietly: man too jot saroop hai. On the out-breath: know your origin. You don't need to work out what that means in two minutes. Just turn toward the question of where your life came from, and stay there, gently. If something critical about yourself shows up, set it beside the line and let the line be louder. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on the out-breath instead. The bell holds the time.
You are the form of light. Man too jot saroop hai: O mind, you are the form of light; recognize your origin. Today's word.
screen: `YOU ARE THE FORM OF LIGHT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: you are light. That closes this week, from Guru Angad's few lines to Guru Amar Das's call to the mind. Today, the next time you put yourself down, answer with the line: man too jot saroop hai. Day one thousand one hundred eighty-three.

howItsDone: This line of Guru Amar Das from Raga Asa is often sung in kirtan and quoted in katha at the gurdwara; some Sikhs keep it as a reminder when they recite or reflect on their own.

original.note: the form of light: Guru Amar Das's words to the mind in Raga Asa.
